name: Tunisia
summary: A red field with a white disc containing a red crescent around a red five-pointed star. Introduced by the Bey of Tunis in 1831, it is one of the oldest flags in the Arab world.
origin: Tunisia was an autonomous province of the Ottoman Empire under the Husainid beys. After the Ottoman-Egyptian fleet was destroyed at the Battle of Navarino in 1827, Al-Husayn II ibn Mahmud ordered a distinct flag for Tunisian ships, adopted in 1831.
The flag remained in use under the French protectorate (1881–1956) and after independence. Its proportions were standardised in 1999, and Article 4 of the 2014 Constitution describes it.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of martyrs; also the Ottoman red.

symbols.name: Disc
symbols.description: A white circle in the centre.
symbols.meaning: Commonly said to represent the sun, or peace.

symbols.name: Crescent and star
symbols.description: A red crescent curving around a red star inside the disc.
symbols.meaning: The unity of Muslims; inherited from Ottoman symbolism.

history.label: Flag of the beylik and republic

facts: It is the oldest flag still in use in the Arab world.
Turkey's flag has the same colours but no disc and a different crescent placement.
The 1999 law fixed the disc's diameter at one-third of the flag's length.
clues: A red crescent and star inside a white disc on a red field.
Introduced in 1831 after a fleet was destroyed at Navarino.
Used through a French protectorate and into independence.
